target.statement: EB-GAD AUROC = 91.4 on Facebook (tied-best with TAM), reproduced by the training-free EB-GAD pipeline
target.dataset: Facebook (attributed social graph, standard GAD benchmark)

compute.basis: Paper reports the full run behind a Table 1 cell takes 8 s on 16 CPU threads for Facebook (small graph, no training, closed-form eigendecomposition + EB fit); the rest is install and dataset download, so a few tens of minutes on a laptop.

blockers: Code repo is anonymized/possibly not yet public at review time
Selector cutoffs are implementation defaults tuned on these benchmarks (transferability caveat, but not a reproduction blocker)
title: Graph Anomaly Detection as Finite-Horizon Control: Training-Free Scoring via Empirical Bayes
